name: Generic plant equipment
description: A small starter for any workshop or plant: inspection templates and log-parameter presets for pumps, motors, and HVAC units. Edit or add your own after loading.

rows.label: Visual condition and leaks
rows.hint: Walk around the unit, base, and seals.

rows.label: Unusual noise or vibration
rows.hint: Compare to the last running condition.

rows.label: Suction and discharge isolation valves in the intended position
rows.hint: Record as-left in remarks.

rows.label: Coupling / guard in place and secure
rows.hint: Do not remove a guard while running.

rows.label: Operating readings recorded in the log book
rows.hint: Flow, pressure, and temperature if fitted.

rows.label: Nameplate readable; mounting secure
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: Cooling vents clear; no abnormal heat
rows.hint: Qualitative unless a limit is set.

rows.label: Terminal box cover on; no loose glands
rows.hint: Isolate before opening a box.

rows.label: Unusual noise or vibration
rows.hint: Compare to the last running condition.

rows.label: Current or temperature reading recorded
rows.hint: Use the Reading column if taken.

rows.label: Filter condition and differential pressure
rows.hint: Record DP in the Reading column if a gauge is fitted.

rows.label: Drains clear; no standing water
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: Fans run; no abnormal noise
rows.hint: Listen and observe.

rows.label: Supply and space temperatures acceptable
rows.hint: Compare to the current setpoint.

rows.label: Area around the unit left clean and accessible
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: Work completed as described
rows.hint: Write what was done in remarks.

rows.label: Parts or consumables used, if any
rows.hint: List in remarks.

rows.label: Equipment left in a safe running or isolated state
rows.hint: Record as-left.

rows.label: Area cleaned; tools removed
rows.hint: Visual check.

name: Semiconductor fab utilities
description: Optional starter: FAT, SAT, and installation record templates plus log-parameter presets for typical fab utility systems (chillers, CDA, UPW, PCW, exhaust, cleanroom HVAC, BMS). Generic practice prompts only — not a site procedure.

rows.label: CHW-F01 — Nameplate data matches the approved submittal (model, capacity, voltage, refrigerant or glycol type).
rows.hint: Transcribe the nameplate and compare to the approved submittal, not to memory.

rows.label: CHW-F02 — Visual inspection for shipping damage, corrosion, loose parts, and open nozzles left uncapped.
rows.hint: Walk the unit on receipt. Note damage on the punch list before installation.

rows.label: CHW-F03 — Factory wiring and terminal labeling match the schematic supplied with the unit.
rows.hint: Spot-check terminal marks against the vendor schematic. Record the schematic revision.

rows.label: CHW-F04 — Control panel powers up; local controller or HMI software version is recorded.
rows.hint: Record version or backup filename. Keep a copy outside this workbook.

rows.label: CHW-F05 — Specified safety devices are present and identified (for example high pressure, low pressure, flow or freeze protection, as applicable).
rows.hint: Presence and tagging check. Trip testing is typically SAT unless a factory report already covers it.

rows.label: CHW-F06 — Factory run-test or performance report is present if the purchase order required one.
rows.hint: File the vendor report. Do not copy vendor curves into this sheet.

rows.label: CHW-F07 — Instruments and valves are tagged; calibration certificates are collected where required.
rows.hint: Tick off against the instrument list. File certificates by tag.

rows.label: CHW-F08 — Communication option and protocol (for example BACnet or Modbus) match the BMS design.
rows.hint: Confirm card type against the controls design. Final addressing is a SAT item.

rows.label: CHW-F09 — O&M manual, spare-parts list, and lifting or anchorage details are included or already received.
rows.hint: List missing documents on the punch list.

rows.label: CHW-S01 — Unit is installed, anchored, labeled, and has the agreed service clearances.
rows.hint: Visual check against the approved layout.

rows.label: CHW-S02 — Electrical supply, phase rotation, and protective earth are checked before first start.
rows.hint: Record the method used. Follow site electrical permit rules.

rows.label: CHW-S03 — Chilled-water and heat-rejection circuits are flushed, filled, vented, and strainers cleaned after flush.
rows.hint: Record flush method and duration. Inspect strainer baskets before the first loaded run.

rows.label: CHW-S04 — Pumps rotate in the correct direction; flow and differential pressure are recorded at a noted operating point.
rows.hint: Enter readings in Actual. Leave Acceptance blank until the project spec is agreed.

rows.label: CHW-S05 — Chiller starts, stops, and unloads or stages in response to load or a simulated load signal.
rows.hint: Note whether the test used real load or a simulated signal.

rows.label: CHW-S06 — Entering and leaving chilled-water temperatures are recorded under a noted load condition.
rows.hint: Record load context. Do not invent a standard limit.

rows.label: CHW-S07 — Safety devices and interlocks trip and reset as expected (for example flow loss, emergency stop).
rows.hint: Test only with a safe, agreed method.

rows.label: CHW-S08 — No unexplained leak, abnormal noise, or abnormal vibration during the site run.
rows.hint: Walk the machine and piping during the run. Raise punches for anything unexplained.

rows.label: CHW-S09 — BMS or FMCS shows run status, fault, and key temperatures, and can issue the designed enable or setpoint.
rows.hint: Cross-reference the point-to-point and alarm sheets.

rows.label: CHW-S10 — Lead-lag or standby staging is demonstrated if more than one unit is installed.
rows.hint: Use a designed test mode. Record which unit took over.

rows.label: CHW-S11 — Insulation, drain routing, valve tagging, and flow-arrow marking are complete.
rows.hint: Visual walk-down.

rows.label: CHW-S12 — As-left setpoints are written on the setpoint sheet before the vendor leaves site.
rows.hint: Use sheet 09-As-Left-Setpoints. Values come from the project spec or a signed decision.

rows.label: INST-01 — Equipment received and inspected against the packing list; damage recorded.
rows.hint: Walk the unit on receipt.

rows.label: INST-02 — Placed, leveled, and anchored per the approved layout, with agreed service clearances.
rows.hint: Visual check against the approved layout.

rows.label: INST-03 — Labels, tags, and flow arrows applied as specified.
rows.hint: Walk-down.

rows.label: INST-04 — Mechanical connections are complete and supported.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-05 — Electrical power and protective earth are terminated; isolation is identified.
rows.hint: Follow site electrical permit rules.

rows.label: INST-06 — Control and instrument wiring is terminated and tagged.
rows.hint: Spot-check tags against the point list if one exists.

rows.label: INST-07 — Insulation, cladding, or guards are installed where designed.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-08 — Drains, vents, and relief paths are present and routed safely.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-09 — The area around the equipment is clear for service and left clean.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-10 — As-built mark-ups started; outstanding install items are listed.
rows.hint: Record drawing IDs in remarks if used.

rows.label: CDA-F01 — Compressor package nameplate (capacity, design pressure, and oil-free statement if specified) matches the approved submittal.
rows.hint: Transcribe the nameplate and compare to the submittal.

rows.label: CDA-F02 — Dryer type and the specified dew-point class or rating match the approved submittal.
rows.hint: Record the specified class in Acceptance later. Do not assume a number here.

rows.label: CDA-F03 — Filter housings of the specified grades are fitted and oriented for the correct flow direction.
rows.hint: Check arrows and element type against the approved bill of materials.

rows.label: CDA-F04 — Auto-drains are fitted on the receiver and filter housings as designed.
rows.hint: Presence check. Function is confirmed at SAT.

rows.label: CDA-F05 — Safety-valve and pressure-vessel documentation is collected where it applies.
rows.hint: File certificates with the project records. Note document IDs in Remarks.

rows.label: CDA-F06 — A dew-point sample point and isolation valves are present as shown on the vendor drawing.
rows.hint: Compare the skid to the drawing. Missing sample points become punches.

rows.label: CDA-F07 — Control-panel software version and the list of local alarms are recorded.
rows.hint: Keep a vendor backup outside this workbook. Do not store passwords here.

rows.label: CDA-F08 — Factory test report is attached if the contract required one.
rows.hint: File, do not re-type, the vendor report.

rows.label: CDA-F09 — Consumables list (elements, and desiccant if used) is included.
rows.hint: Useful later for the handover spare-parts list.

templates.name: SAT / site commissioning — Clean dry air

rows.label: CDA-S01 — Package is installed, leveled, and labeled; the intake path is clear and suitable for the specified air quality.
rows.hint: Visual check. Note any contamination risk at the intake.

rows.label: CDA-S02 — Receiver and distribution piping have been blown down or flushed by the agreed method, then leak-checked after hook-up.
rows.hint: Record the method. Walk the header and branches, not only the skid.

rows.label: CDA-S03 — The system reaches the specified pressure and the result of a hold or decay check (if used) is recorded.
rows.hint: Enter the project pressure in Acceptance. Record observed pressure and hold time in Actual.

rows.label: CDA-S04 — Dew point is measured at the agreed sample point under a noted flow or load condition.
rows.hint: Note analyser type and calibration due date. Load context belongs in Remarks.

rows.label: CDA-S05 — Dryer operation is normal; pre-filter and after-filter differential pressures are recorded.
rows.hint: Record DP and element condition. Change criteria belong in setpoints or PM notes once agreed.

rows.label: CDA-S06 — Auto-drains operate; no standing water is left in receivers or known low points.
rows.hint: Observe a drain cycle. Check low-point drains on the distribution header.

rows.label: CDA-S07 — Lead-lag or backup compressor auto-start is demonstrated.
rows.hint: Use the designed test or a simulated lead fault. Record which machine started.

rows.label: CDA-S08 — Pressure and dew-point alarms to the BMS are tested.
rows.hint: Cross-reference the alarm sheet. Record whether an interlock (not just an alarm) is designed.

rows.label: CDA-S09 — A representative point-of-use drop is spot-checked for pressure and, if specified, dew point.
rows.hint: Choose a far or critical drop if the project identifies one.

rows.label: CDA-S10 — Isolation valves, check valves, and any bypasses are tagged and left in the intended position.
rows.hint: Record as-left bypass positions if a bypass is open.

rows.label: CDA-S11 — Plant-room noise, vibration, and heat-rejection path are acceptable for the installed location.
rows.hint: Qualitative check unless the project states a limit.

rows.label: CDA-S12 — As-left pressure and dryer settings are recorded before the vendor leaves.
rows.hint: Use sheet 09-As-Left-Setpoints.

rows.label: INST-01 — Equipment received and inspected against the packing list; damage recorded.
rows.hint: Walk the unit on receipt.

rows.label: INST-02 — Placed, leveled, and anchored per the approved layout, with agreed service clearances.
rows.hint: Visual check against the approved layout.

rows.label: INST-03 — Labels, tags, and flow arrows applied as specified.
rows.hint: Walk-down.

rows.label: INST-04 — Mechanical connections are complete and supported.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-05 — Electrical power and protective earth are terminated; isolation is identified.
rows.hint: Follow site electrical permit rules.

rows.label: INST-06 — Control and instrument wiring is terminated and tagged.
rows.hint: Spot-check tags against the point list if one exists.

rows.label: INST-07 — Insulation, cladding, or guards are installed where designed.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-08 — Drains, vents, and relief paths are present and routed safely.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-09 — The area around the equipment is clear for service and left clean.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-10 — As-built mark-ups started; outstanding install items are listed.
rows.hint: Record drawing IDs in remarks if used.

rows.label: UPW-F01 — Skid or major-equipment nameplates match the approved submittal.
rows.hint: Transcribe model and serials. Compare to the submittal and equipment list.

rows.label: UPW-F02 — Declared materials of construction for wetted parts are consistent with the specification.
rows.hint: Record what the vendor declared. Do not add material rules here.

rows.label: UPW-F03 — Quality and process instruments (for example resistivity, TOC, flow, temperature) match the instrument list for model and range.
rows.hint: Tick against the instrument index. File calibration certificates.

rows.label: UPW-F04 — Factory pressure or hydrostatic test records are collected where provided.
rows.hint: File the records; note certificate IDs.

rows.label: UPW-F05 — Control narrative, I/O list, and software version are received and the version is recorded.
rows.hint: Store backups outside this workbook. No passwords in this file.

rows.label: UPW-F06 — UV, filters, and polishing stages are present as designed; lamp or filter identifiers are recorded.
rows.hint: Presence and identification check.

rows.label: UPW-F07 — Sample valves are installed at the locations shown on the skid drawing or P&ID.
rows.hint: Walk the skid with the drawing. Missing sample points become punches.

rows.label: UPW-F08 — Quality-divert or dump valves are present, tagged, and shown on the drawing.
rows.hint: Function is demonstrated at SAT. FAT is a presence and documentation check.

rows.label: UPW-F09 — Any factory cleanliness or flush procedure that was used is documented.
rows.hint: Keep the vendor description as an attachment. Do not paste a proprietary recipe here.

rows.label: UPW-F10 — A skid dead-leg or drainability review against the P&ID is noted, including discrepancies.
rows.hint: Drawing-vs-skid walk. Site loop walk-down is a SAT item.

rows.label: UPW-S01 — Loop and equipment are installed, supported, and labeled; slope and drainability are visually checked.
rows.hint: Walk the loop with the as-built or red-line drawing.

rows.label: UPW-S02 — The system is flushed and started using the agreed project cleanliness procedure, and the method and duration are recorded.
rows.hint: Record what was actually done. Do not copy a generic recipe into Acceptance.

rows.label: UPW-S03 — Recirculation flow and loop temperature are recorded at a stated operating mode.
rows.hint: Note the mode. Enter project bands in Acceptance when known.

rows.label: UPW-S04 — Specified product-quality readings are recorded at the agreed sample points (for example makeup outlet, use point, or return).
rows.hint: List only the parameters the project specifies. Leave limits blank until the spec is entered.

rows.label: UPW-S05 — Quality-divert or dump interlock is demonstrated by an agreed, safe test method.
rows.hint: Record the method. Do not skip this because the quality reading looks fine.

rows.label: UPW-S06 — UV status and runtime are recorded; the lamp-change method is reviewed with the operator.
rows.hint: Training can be referenced on the handover sheet.

rows.label: UPW-S07 — Filter differential pressures are recorded and the change criterion is written into the setpoint or PM notes.
rows.hint: Do not invent a DP limit. Use the agreed project or vendor criterion.

rows.label: UPW-S08 — Sample points are accessible, can be flushed, and the sample method is agreed.
rows.hint: Confirm that operators can actually reach and use the points.

rows.label: UPW-S09 — Low-flow, high-temperature, and analyser-fault alarms are tested through to the BMS.
rows.hint: Cross-reference the alarm sheet.

rows.label: UPW-S10 — Standby pump or other designed redundancy auto-changeover is demonstrated if provided.
rows.hint: Use the designed test method. Record which equipment took over.

rows.label: UPW-S11 — A leak and dead-leg walk-down finds no unidentified branches, stagnant legs, or leaks.
rows.hint: Raise punches if a drawing change is needed.

rows.label: UPW-S12 — As-left quality setpoints and divert limits are recorded from the project specification or a signed site decision.
rows.hint: Use sheet 09-As-Left-Setpoints. Leave cells blank rather than guessing.

rows.label: INST-01 — Equipment received and inspected against the packing list; damage recorded.
rows.hint: Walk the unit on receipt.

rows.label: INST-02 — Placed, leveled, and anchored per the approved layout, with agreed service clearances.
rows.hint: Visual check against the approved layout.

rows.label: INST-03 — Labels, tags, and flow arrows applied as specified.
rows.hint: Walk-down.

rows.label: INST-04 — Mechanical connections are complete and supported.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-05 — Electrical power and protective earth are terminated; isolation is identified.
rows.hint: Follow site electrical permit rules.

rows.label: INST-06 — Control and instrument wiring is terminated and tagged.
rows.hint: Spot-check tags against the point list if one exists.

rows.label: INST-07 — Insulation, cladding, or guards are installed where designed.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-08 — Drains, vents, and relief paths are present and routed safely.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-09 — The area around the equipment is clear for service and left clean.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-10 — As-built mark-ups started; outstanding install items are listed.
rows.hint: Record drawing IDs in remarks if used.

rows.label: PCW-F01 — Major equipment nameplates (pumps, heat exchangers, tanks) match the approved submittal.
rows.hint: Transcribe model, impeller or duty if shown, and serials.

rows.label: PCW-F02 — Declared materials and elastomer compatibility are consistent with the specified process-cooling fluid.
rows.hint: Record the declared materials. Compatibility is a design responsibility, not decided in this checklist.

rows.label: PCW-F03 — Control valves, instruments, and relief or fill equipment on the skid match the drawing and instrument list.
rows.hint: Presence and tagging check. File calibration certificates where required.

rows.label: PCW-F04 — Factory pressure-test records for exchangers, tanks, or coils are collected where provided.
rows.hint: File certificates; note IDs in Remarks.

rows.label: PCW-F05 — Control narrative and software version for any packaged controller are received.
rows.hint: Backup stored outside this workbook.

rows.label: PCW-F06 — Spare-parts list and O&M manuals are present.
rows.hint: Missing documents go to the punch list.

rows.label: PCW-F07 — Heat-exchanger nameplate duty is consistent with the approved submittal (record nameplate only).
rows.hint: Do not re-rate the exchanger on this sheet.

rows.label: PCW-F08 — Shipping damage, open nozzles, and flange-face condition are inspected on receipt.
rows.hint: Raise punches before installation.

templates.name: SAT / site commissioning — Process cooling water

rows.label: PCW-S01 — Loop is installed, labeled, supported, and insulated as designed; drains and vents are present at high and low points.
rows.hint: Visual walk-down against the drawing.

rows.label: PCW-S02 — The loop is flushed, filled with the specified fluid, treated if specified, and vented.
rows.hint: Record fluid type and any treatment used. Do not invent a chemistry target.

rows.label: PCW-S03 — Pumps rotate correctly; supply and return pressures, differential pressure, and flow are recorded at a noted operating point.
rows.hint: Enter project bands in Acceptance when known.

rows.label: PCW-S04 — Supply and return temperatures, and exchanger approach if applicable, are recorded under a noted load condition.
rows.hint: Note whether load was process, simulated, or building-side only.

rows.label: PCW-S05 — Temperature-control valve or variable-speed response is demonstrated in both directions.
rows.hint: Stroke or speed-change test. Confirm BMS setpoint tracking if designed.

rows.label: PCW-S06 — Standby pump auto-changeover is demonstrated if provided.
rows.hint: Use the designed test. Record the transfer.

rows.label: PCW-S07 — Strainer and filter differential pressures are recorded after flush and after a first run.
rows.hint: Clean or replace elements if required, then record as-left DP.

rows.label: PCW-S08 — Low-flow, high-temperature, and pump-fault alarms or interlocks are tested to the BMS and to any designed process interlock.
rows.hint: Do not trip tools without an agreed method.

rows.label: PCW-S09 — A leak walk is completed on headers, branches, and hose or tool-hook-up points that are in scope.
rows.hint: Scope the walk in Remarks (plant only vs hook-up drops).

rows.label: PCW-S10 — Water-quality or treatment readings required by the project (for example conductivity or inhibitor residual) are recorded.
rows.hint: Leave Acceptance blank until the project chemistry spec is entered.

rows.label: PCW-S11 — As-left temperature, pressure, and control settings are recorded before the vendor leaves.
rows.hint: Use sheet 09-As-Left-Setpoints.

rows.label: INST-01 — Equipment received and inspected against the packing list; damage recorded.
rows.hint: Walk the unit on receipt.

rows.label: INST-02 — Placed, leveled, and anchored per the approved layout, with agreed service clearances.
rows.hint: Visual check against the approved layout.

rows.label: INST-03 — Labels, tags, and flow arrows applied as specified.
rows.hint: Walk-down.

rows.label: INST-04 — Mechanical connections are complete and supported.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-05 — Electrical power and protective earth are terminated; isolation is identified.
rows.hint: Follow site electrical permit rules.

rows.label: INST-06 — Control and instrument wiring is terminated and tagged.
rows.hint: Spot-check tags against the point list if one exists.

rows.label: INST-07 — Insulation, cladding, or guards are installed where designed.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-08 — Drains, vents, and relief paths are present and routed safely.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-09 — The area around the equipment is clear for service and left clean.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-10 — As-built mark-ups started; outstanding install items are listed.
rows.hint: Record drawing IDs in remarks if used.

rows.label: EXH-F01 — Fan and scrubber or abatement nameplates match the approved submittal (including materials where declared).
rows.hint: Transcribe nameplates. Compare to the submittal.

rows.label: EXH-F02 — Scrubber internals that can be inspected on receipt (packing, mist eliminator, spray headers, as applicable) are present and undamaged.
rows.hint: Do not dismantle beyond what vendor or site safety rules allow.

rows.label: EXH-F03 — Recirculation pumps, dosing points, pH or other specified analysers, and level devices are present and tagged.
rows.hint: Presence check against the P&ID or skid drawing.

rows.label: EXH-F04 — Factory inspection or performance report is attached if the contract required one.
rows.hint: File the vendor report.

rows.label: EXH-F05 — Control panel software version and local interlock list are recorded.
rows.hint: Backup stored outside this workbook.

rows.label: EXH-F06 — Access platforms, nozzles, and sample or instrument ports match the drawing.
rows.hint: Missing ports become punches.

rows.label: EXH-F07 — Chemical compatibility documentation and SDS for any vendor-supplied reagents are received.
rows.hint: SDS belong in the site chemical file, not pasted into this workbook.

rows.label: EXH-F08 — Shipping damage, liner condition (if visible), and flange condition are inspected on receipt.
rows.hint: Raise punches before installation.

rows.label: EXH-S01 — Fans, ducts, and abatement equipment are installed, supported, labeled, and accessible for service.
rows.hint: Visual check, including drain routing and spill containment if designed.

rows.label: EXH-S02 — Fan rotation is correct; airflow or duct static is recorded at a noted operating mode.
rows.hint: Enter the project target in Acceptance when known. Record instrument and method used.

rows.label: EXH-S03 — Redundant or backup fan start is demonstrated if provided.
rows.hint: Use the designed test method.

rows.label: EXH-S04 — For a wet scrubber, recirculation flow, level control, and specified chemistry readings (for example pH) are recorded in a stable run.
rows.hint: Leave chemistry limits blank until the project or permit basis is entered.

rows.label: EXH-S05 — Dosing, makeup, and blowdown (if provided) operate without overflow or loss of seal.
rows.hint: Observe a makeup or blowdown cycle if it can be done safely.

rows.label: EXH-S06 — Designed interlocks are tested (for example fan-fail, low recirculation, out-of-range chemistry), including any agreed effect on upstream tools or dampers.
rows.hint: Never trip a process tool without an agreed, safe method and process-owner consent.

rows.label: EXH-S07 — Bypass dampers, isolation dampers, and access doors are tagged and left in the intended position.
rows.hint: Record as-left damper positions if they are not obvious.

rows.label: EXH-S08 — A visual leak, corrosion, and liquid-leak walk is completed on ducts, pumps, and chemical lines in scope.
rows.hint: Raise punches for staining, drips, or damaged flex connectors.

rows.label: EXH-S09 — Emission or stack monitoring points, if specified, are accessible and correctly located per the drawing.
rows.hint: This is an access and location check, not an emissions certification.

rows.label: EXH-S10 — Alarms for fan fail, low flow, and chemistry (if used) are tested through to the BMS.
rows.hint: Cross-reference the alarm sheet.

rows.label: EXH-S11 — As-left fan, damper, and chemistry-control settings are recorded before the vendor leaves.
rows.hint: Use sheet 09-As-Left-Setpoints.

rows.label: INST-01 — Equipment received and inspected against the packing list; damage recorded.
rows.hint: Walk the unit on receipt.

rows.label: INST-02 — Placed, leveled, and anchored per the approved layout, with agreed service clearances.
rows.hint: Visual check against the approved layout.

rows.label: INST-03 — Labels, tags, and flow arrows applied as specified.
rows.hint: Walk-down.

rows.label: INST-04 — Mechanical connections are complete and supported.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-05 — Electrical power and protective earth are terminated; isolation is identified.
rows.hint: Follow site electrical permit rules.

rows.label: INST-06 — Control and instrument wiring is terminated and tagged.
rows.hint: Spot-check tags against the point list if one exists.

rows.label: INST-07 — Insulation, cladding, or guards are installed where designed.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-08 — Drains, vents, and relief paths are present and routed safely.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-09 — The area around the equipment is clear for service and left clean.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-10 — As-built mark-ups started; outstanding install items are listed.
rows.hint: Record drawing IDs in remarks if used.

rows.label: HVAC-F01 — AHU, make-up unit, and FFU nameplates or submittal data match what was approved (including filter grade if stated).
rows.hint: Transcribe nameplates or packing lists. Compare to the approved submittal.

rows.label: HVAC-F02 — Filters are the specified grade, undamaged, and installed in the correct orientation if they ship with the unit.
rows.hint: Visual inspection. Integrity testing, if required, is a specialist or SAT item.

rows.label: HVAC-F03 — Factory functional check of fans, cooling, heating, and dampers is documented if the contract required a FAT.
rows.hint: File the vendor report.

rows.label: HVAC-F04 — Control panel or FFU-controller software version is recorded; the point list is received.
rows.hint: Backup stored outside this workbook.

rows.label: HVAC-F05 — Access sections, drains, and instrument tappings shown on the drawing are present.
rows.hint: Missing tappings become punches.

rows.label: HVAC-F06 — Shipping damage to casings, coils, flex connectors, and fan decks is inspected on receipt.
rows.hint: Raise punches before installation or cleanroom protocol changeover.

rows.label: HVAC-F07 — Material and finish declarations (for example cleanroom-side finishes) are consistent with the specification.
rows.hint: Record what was declared. Do not add a finish standard here.

templates.name: SAT / site commissioning — Cleanroom HVAC / FFU

rows.label: HVAC-S01 — Units and FFUs are installed, labeled, and accessible; condensate drains are trapped and free-flowing where designed.
rows.hint: Visual check. Pour-test a drain only if site rules allow.

rows.label: HVAC-S02 — Fans and FFUs run; speed or stage commands from the local controller and from the BMS work as designed.
rows.hint: Spot-check a sample of FFUs if the population is large. Record the sample size in Remarks.

rows.label: HVAC-S03 — Supply, return, and exhaust relationships are in the intended direction; obvious reverse-flow or dead zones are noted.
rows.hint: Facilities functional check, not a formal airflow-visualization study. If a specialist study is required, record who will do it.

rows.label: HVAC-S04 — Room or space pressure polarity and cascade are recorded at the agreed doors or rooms.
rows.hint: Enter project targets in Acceptance when known. Record door states during the reading.

rows.label: HVAC-S05 — Temperature and humidity are recorded at the agreed locations under a noted operating mode.
rows.hint: Do not invent a band. Use the project environmental spec.

rows.label: HVAC-S06 — Filter installation is confirmed (grade, damage, seating). If an integrity or classification test is in scope, the specialist report is referenced rather than repeating that procedure here.
rows.hint: Record support conditions and the report ID. Do not copy test methods from a standard into this sheet.

rows.label: HVAC-S07 — AHU cooling, heating, humidification, and dehumidification (as installed) respond in the correct direction to a setpoint change.
rows.hint: One change in each installed direction is enough for this check.

rows.label: HVAC-S08 — Door, airlock, or interlock functions that are part of the facilities scope operate as designed.
rows.hint: Test only the interlocks that are actually installed and in facilities scope.

rows.label: HVAC-S09 — Alarms for FFU or fan fail, pressure loss, and temperature or humidity out of range are tested to the BMS.
rows.hint: Cross-reference the alarm sheet.

rows.label: HVAC-S10 — Filter differential-pressure readings are recorded and the monitoring method (local gauge, BMS, or both) is noted.
rows.hint: Change criteria belong in setpoints or the PM plan once agreed.

rows.label: HVAC-S11 — As-left room setpoints, FFU speeds or stages, and alarm delays are recorded before the vendor leaves.
rows.hint: Use sheet 09-As-Left-Setpoints.

rows.label: INST-01 — Equipment received and inspected against the packing list; damage recorded.
rows.hint: Walk the unit on receipt.

rows.label: INST-02 — Placed, leveled, and anchored per the approved layout, with agreed service clearances.
rows.hint: Visual check against the approved layout.

rows.label: INST-03 — Labels, tags, and flow arrows applied as specified.
rows.hint: Walk-down.

rows.label: INST-04 — Mechanical connections are complete and supported.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-05 — Electrical power and protective earth are terminated; isolation is identified.
rows.hint: Follow site electrical permit rules.

rows.label: INST-06 — Control and instrument wiring is terminated and tagged.
rows.hint: Spot-check tags against the point list if one exists.

rows.label: INST-07 — Insulation, cladding, or guards are installed where designed.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-08 — Drains, vents, and relief paths are present and routed safely.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-09 — The area around the equipment is clear for service and left clean.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-10 — As-built mark-ups started; outstanding install items are listed.
rows.hint: Record drawing IDs in remarks if used.

rows.label: BMS-F01 — Controller or server hardware and licensed software versions match the approved controls submittal.
rows.hint: Record product names and versions. Keep licence keys out of this workbook.

rows.label: BMS-F02 — A point database or export matching the approved I/O or point schedule is received.
rows.hint: File the export. As-built addressing is confirmed on the point-to-point sheet at SAT.

rows.label: BMS-F03 — Graphics package or a typical graphic template is received for review.
rows.hint: Review navigation and required systems. Live graphics are a SAT item.

rows.label: BMS-F04 — Alarm class or priority scheme in the submittal is documented and agreed in principle.
rows.hint: Final priorities are a site decision; record them at SAT.

rows.label: BMS-F05 — Historian or trend licence and intended log interval are stated in the submittal.
rows.hint: Confirm later that the agreed points actually log.

rows.label: BMS-F06 — Backup-and-restore method is documented by the vendor.
rows.hint: The restore itself is demonstrated at SAT.

rows.label: BMS-F07 — User-role model (who can command, who can change setpoints, who can only view) is described.
rows.hint: Do not write passwords or personal accounts into this workbook.

rows.label: BMS-F08 — Interface list to packaged equipment (chillers, dryers, UPW, scrubbers, FFU controllers) is complete.
rows.hint: Each interface is then proven on SAT, system by system.

rows.label: BMS-S01 — Controllers, servers, networks, and operator workstations are installed, time-synchronised, and running the recorded software versions.
rows.hint: Record time source. A wrong clock corrupts the commissioning record.

rows.label: BMS-S02 — A sample of points from each utility system is verified field-to-graphic (and to the historian if in scope).
rows.hint: Use sheet 06-Point-to-Point. State the sample rule in Remarks if not 100%.

rows.label: BMS-S03 — Graphics for each in-scope system navigate correctly, show live data, and display the alarm banner or equivalent.
rows.hint: Walk a user through each system graphic.

rows.label: BMS-S04 — Alarm routing and notification (workstation, email, SMS, or other designed path) are tested with a benign test alarm.
rows.hint: Do not use a live emergency to test routing. Record the receiving role, not a personal number.

rows.label: BMS-S05 — Agreed points are historized at the agreed interval; a gap or collection failure is visible to the operator if that function exists.
rows.hint: Export a short trend as evidence. Store it with the project files.

rows.label: BMS-S06 — User access levels work as designed; a view-only user cannot change a setpoint.
rows.hint: Use test accounts. Never store real passwords in this file.

rows.label: BMS-S07 — Backup and restore are demonstrated, or a witnessed backup is taken and the restore procedure is reviewed if a live restore is not allowed.
rows.hint: Record backup filename, date, and storage location — not credentials.

rows.label: BMS-S08 — Fail-safe or comms-loss behavior for each interface is documented and, where safe, demonstrated.
rows.hint: If a live test is not safe, record the designed behavior and why the test was deferred.

rows.label: BMS-S09 — Setpoint-change audit trail or activity log, if the product provides one, is confirmed to be on.
rows.hint: Useful at handover when settings are questioned later.

rows.label: BMS-S10 — An operator walk-through or training session is completed and recorded on the handover sheet.
rows.hint: Attendance belongs with handover evidence.

rows.label: BMS-S11 — As-left global settings (alarm delays, lockouts, historian interval, notification lists) are recorded.
rows.hint: Use sheet 09-As-Left-Setpoints. Name roles, not personal phone numbers, if that is more stable.

rows.label: INST-01 — Equipment received and inspected against the packing list; damage recorded.
rows.hint: Walk the unit on receipt.

rows.label: INST-02 — Placed, leveled, and anchored per the approved layout, with agreed service clearances.
rows.hint: Visual check against the approved layout.

rows.label: INST-03 — Labels, tags, and flow arrows applied as specified.
rows.hint: Walk-down.

rows.label: INST-04 — Mechanical connections are complete and supported.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-05 — Electrical power and protective earth are terminated; isolation is identified.
rows.hint: Follow site electrical permit rules.

rows.label: INST-06 — Control and instrument wiring is terminated and tagged.
rows.hint: Spot-check tags against the point list if one exists.

rows.label: INST-07 — Insulation, cladding, or guards are installed where designed.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-08 — Drains, vents, and relief paths are present and routed safely.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-09 — The area around the equipment is clear for service and left clean.
rows.hint: Visual check.

rows.label: INST-10 — As-built mark-ups started; outstanding install items are listed.
rows.hint: Record drawing IDs in remarks if used.
